title.ko: 요리법 설명: 명령문 · 순서 표현 · 수동태
title.en: explaining recipes: imperatives, sequencers and the passive

explain.ko: 요리법은 명령문과 순서 표현(first, then, after that, finally)으로 씁니다. 명령문은 동사원형으로 시작하고(Chop the onion), 부정은 Don't + 동사원형입니다. 두 동작을 잇는 표현은 before / after + -ing 또는 절입니다(Taste it before you add salt). 일반적인 방법은 수동태로 쓸 수도 있습니다(The onion is chopped and fried). 시간과 온도는 for five minutes, at 180 degrees처럼 전치사로 나타냅니다.
explain.en: Recipes use imperatives and sequencers (first, then, after that, finally). An imperative starts with the base verb (Chop the onion); the negative is Don't + base verb. Link steps with before / after + -ing or a clause (Taste it before you add salt). A method can also be passive (The onion is chopped and fried). Give times and temperatures with prepositions: for five minutes, at 180 degrees.

notes.en: Imperatives have no subject; they begin with the base verb.
